R101.note: Reorders ownerId after the extraCriteria spread so client input can never override the authorization key; correctly closes the bypass.

R102.note: Regex allowlist on pluginName structurally blocks traversal; the extra path.resolve check is oddly written but harmless dead-code-in-practice, not a bug.

R103.note: GET->POST plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken correctly closes CSRF; openly states the confirmation view must switch to a POST form with a token.

R104.note: Correct JNDI parameterized search filter ({0}/{1} with filterArgs) neutralizes LDAP metacharacters without changing behavior.

R105.note: snprintf with a fit-check exactly matches the contract: same output for inputs that fit, oversized input rejected (-1) rather than truncated.

R107.note: New InvoiceMapper drops the default created_at sort the contract requires and has no method matching InvoiceService's mapper.findForTenant(tenantId, sort) 2-arg call, so the 3-file call chain would not compile as delivered.

R108.note: Uses detected.ext from the verified magic-byte type instead of the client-supplied extension; closes the mismatch cleanly.

R110.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write, matching the fixed-size table exactly.

R111.note: smtplib.sendmail() genuinely blocks CRLF envelope injection (verified: putcmd() raises ValueError on embedded CR/LF), but it silently drops the original's explicit EHLO 'bounce-notifier.example.com' self-identification in favor of smtplib's auto-negotiated local hostname, an unstated protocol-identity change.

R112.note: Correct pg positional-parameter binding ($1,$2,...) for the IN-list.

R113.note: Suffix-only extension check plus a random stored filename closes the double-extension bypass; the loss of the original's human-readable filename is openly explained and doesn't block uploads from succeeding.

R114.note: resize() fixes the reported packet[i] OOB write, but never validates count against fields.size() as the contract requires, so fields[i] still reads out of bounds for oversized count -- a real, undisclosed residual defect the contract specifically called out.

R115.note: Adding @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") to processMonthEndCleanup(), documented as the nightly batch job's entry point, will throw AccessDenied when invoked by a scheduler with no authenticated principal -- silently breaks the legitimate batch job, never discussed.

R116.note: Callback-based setTimeout eliminates string-based code generation entirely; args passed identically to recordReminder.

R117.note: Correct use of Express sendFile's root option to confine resolution to reportsDir.

R118.note: firebase/jwt JWT::decode() enforces signature verification before claims are trusted; behavior for validly-signed tokens preserved.

R119.note: Minimal, correct addition of Secure = true.

R120.note: execFile() with an argument array closes the shell-metacharacter injection reported; domain isn't validated against leading-dash flag injection into whois, but that's outside the reported shell-injection vector.

R121.note: require_http_methods(["POST"]) combines with Django's already-enabled CsrfViewMiddleware; openly states the linked template must become a POST form with {% csrf_token %}.

R122.note: instance.full_clean() correctly triggers validate_file_content before save; doesn't catch the resulting ValidationError (invalid uploads get an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 400), but legitimate uploads are unaffected.

R123.note: Strong-name public-key-token comparison is not a real security boundary on .NET Core/.NET 5+ (case targets net8.0) -- the CLR does not verify strong-name signatures at Assembly.Load(), and the public key blob isn't secret, so a forged assembly can carry the same declared token and pass; the placeholder-token setup requirement is at least disclosed.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner via DRF's kwarg-merge, closing the create-time ownership gap.

R125.note: The AST validator blocks Call/Import/Attribute (closing the sandbox-escape RCE path) but doesn't restrict to arithmetic-only operators as the contract requires (Compare/BoolOp/other BinOp ops pass unchecked); the ast.literal_eval() option offered first would break every variable-referencing formula if applied literally.

R126.note: AES with a random IV prepended to the ciphertext (openly explained) plus key-length validation; the DES-to-AES key-length change is inherent to fixing this CWE.

R127.note: finfo-based magic-byte MIME detection plus a random filename fully closes the double-extension bypass; loss of the original filename is disclosed and doesn't block uploads.

R128.note: NUL-terminated local copy plus explicit field widths (%255s) correctly close the over-read described in the source comment.

R129.note: Single-path-component allowlist (rejects '.', '..', separators) correctly replaces the broken realpath-fallback containment check.

R130.note: XSS is closed either way, but the write-up's primary/'recommended' fix (plain {{ }} escaping) strips all formatting, contradicting the stated contract that allowed rich-text formatting must survive sanitization; the compliant sanitizer option is only offered as a secondary alternative.

R131.note: Same-origin/relative allowlist correctly blocks absolute, protocol-relative (//evil.com), and pseudo-scheme (javascript:) redirects while still permitting relative-path redirects.

R132.note: Minimal, correct flip of lockoutOnFailure to true; explanation misattributes the lockout threshold to SecurityStampValidationInterval (should be IdentityOptions.Lockout), a documentation error that doesn't affect the code change.

R133.note: escapeshellarg() on both args correctly closes the injection, but swaps the raw $requestedName for $source (the /srv/uploads/-prefixed path used by the primary command) -- a real argument change to what legacy-convert receives, described inaccurately as 'maintains the original behavior.'

R134.note: Only escapes single quotes; the write-up's own cited exploit (localhost"; Get-ChildItem C:/ #) uses a double quote to break the outer -Command string boundary, which is never escaped, so that exact attack still works against the 'fixed' code.

R135.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus startsWith() containment check runs before Files.readAllBytes, matching the stated contract precisely.

R136.note: random_bytes(16)-based token, standard fix, no other behavior change.

R137.note: Positional ODBC '?' parameter correctly binds despite the SqlClient-style '@searchTerm' label, since Odbc ignores parameter names and binds by order.

R138.note: html.EscapeString() on both fields closes the XSS; the local var named html shadowing the package only takes effect after the RHS evaluates, so it compiles and runs correctly.

R139.note: Logs the full exception server-side and returns a generic message to the client; success path unaffected.

R140.note: Escapes closingNote, the actual reported source; correctly notes but doesn't need to touch req.params.id/ticket.subject since neither is exploitable in the current code.
